brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: 4 bases in a 2x2-ish cluster (3 full + 1 half-n) with plain top covers on the three full bases, capped open faces and locked joints; pencil-cup and phone props on the tops show desk use
Classic drawer (drawer:0#1,1#cut) on the cut face of the half-n base at 1,1,0; dressed with a pen and a pencil inside

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at the junction of bases 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0
platform-sm accessory fitted on the mount spike (solid spike was refused by configurator; converted to mount per its steps)

finish.summary: Built a compact desk unit: three full bases plus a half-n base in a tight cluster, top covers forming the desk surface, a classic drawer in the half base (with pen/pencil inside), and at the corner where the three full bases meet a mount spike carrying the small platform (platform-sm). Open faces capped and joints locked; staged with a pencil cup and phone. check_build is clear with no issues.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your compact desk unit — a drawer module plus a corner spike platform — starting by surveying the current layout and parts.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

result.rollback: Nothing in this batch is on the build: one op was refused, so every op in it was undone. Fix or drop the refused op and send the batch again (a refusal with details.steps gives the whole batch with it fixed: send those ops as one apply); refs and offers from this batch do not exist.
